Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • setup.py reads requirements.txt and README.md and defines package metadata, dependencies, and entry points via setuptools.setup(). There is no evidence of install-time command execution, downloading, credential access, or an obfuscated loader.
  • No .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, or custom PEP 517 build-hook files were identified in the provided corpus.
  • entry_points.txt defines scauto = SCAutolib.cli_commands:cli under console_scripts; this requires explicit user execution and is not treated as malicious automatic execution.
  • SCAutolib/__init__.py performs import-time logging setup and defines constants/schemas, but no supply-chain malware behavior such as network exfiltration, credential harvesting, or persistence installation was identified.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • Credential theft: No evidence of broad discovery of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud/CI tokens, wallets, or package-registry tokens.
  • Exfiltration/staging: No evidence of archive staging, temporary harvesting directories, external HTTP uploads, webhooks, suspicious C2 domains, or raw IP endpoints.
  • Persistence: SCAutolib/models/card.py contains logic involving /etc/systemd/system/{service}.service, but it appears tied to the package’s documented virtual smart-card testing functionality and user-triggered operations. Evidence is insufficient to classify it as malicious supply-chain persistence.
  • Lateral movement: No evidence of Kubernetes, Docker socket, cloud metadata access, GitHub Actions/CI token theft, or workflow injection.
  • Stealth/loader behavior: The eval("{0} {1} {2}".format(...)) use in utils.py is for distro version comparison and does not plausibly indicate an obfuscated payload loader. re.compile() and the subprocess wrapper do not constitute malicious stealth/loader evidence.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • SCAutolib/templates/match_for_RHEL-10.png appears to be a small PNG template; the provided evidence does not indicate hidden payload or executable logic.
  • Files listed in SOURCES.txt appear to be package source files, templates, tests, and egg-info metadata; no unexplained native binary or hidden executable was identified.
  • Dependencies in requires.txt generally align with smart-card, CLI, testing, and GUI automation use cases. No clear evidence of malicious dependency insertion or typosquatting was identified.
  • Wheel/sdist mismatch cannot be assessed from a single extracted sdist.
